accuracy.evidence: Fire facts checked: began early on Sunday 2 September 1666 in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane; hot dry summer; timber houses with jettied upper floors over narrow lanes; strong east wind; riverside stores of oil, tar (pitch) and coal; Lord Mayor Bludworth refused early demolition; houses blown up with gunpowder for firebreaks; wind dropped on 5 September; about 13,200 houses, 87 parish churches and St Paul's destroyed; rebuilding in brick and stone with some wider streets. RI.4.3 and RI.5.3 wording quoted from the standard.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented reading slips: sequence taken as cause (then vs because, Sunday as a reason), a single cause when the text gives several (bakery prediction), cause and effect reversed (because/so flips with their own feedback), details listed as reasons, and claims with no textual evidence (proof scene and challenge).

lab_distinct.evidence: Built around one numbered informational text: cause/effect/detail sort around the event, tapping the exact sentence that proves a claim, choosing the connective that shows direction of causation, a procedure where each placed step prints its because, and an arrowed cause chain. The shingle check passes, and the mechanics only make sense for explaining events and ideas.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers by doing: a wrong drop explains why (e.g. 'came before the spread and helped it happen. That makes it a cause'), the proof scene lights the sentence it accepts, the joined sentences collect under the gap as a model list, and the chain is read down its arrows. The done messages confirm the rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Prediction 1 offers the tempting single cause 'The bakery fire was huge' before the sort shows four separate causes. Prediction 2 offers 'then' as a word that explains why; the link scene then rejects then in every sentence with feedback that it only gives the order.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; each wrong answer is tagged and gets a named slip: one cause only, detail not reason, order not reason, cause/effect flipped, no proof from the text, firebreak made too late. Each message says what to look for instead.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade 1.2 with short sentences and one worked example; adult text FK 9.2 (family limits 5.0/10.0). Cards are 2 to 9 words. The text uses everyday words (stores, gaps, top floors leaned out) instead of warehouses, jettied, conflagration.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one move: event/causes/effects, a cause with the fire as example, proof by sentence number, because/so vs then plus chains. Adult paragraphs cover standards, the three-part explanation, named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark: on phones the three sort boxes stack full width with placed cards in two columns; the 10 numbered sentences each get their own tap row; joined sentences list under the gap; firebreak steps get 64 px rows so the step and its reason stay readable; the chain shows 5 arrowed links without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button route (Take a card, then choose a place, or Put back; Sentence 1 to 10 buttons carry the full sentence in their aria-label). Each action updates the canvas aria-label and the live region, including the challenge. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations.
